parts.gloss: you do not (negative second person singular)

literal: Hereafter such things with you who will consult, O heart! Sulking having made, you do not enjoy, see, indeed!
translation: O my heart! Who will consult with you hereafter on such matters? For you prolong your sulking and do not enjoy the pleasure of union when it is offered.
modern: நெஞ்சமே! இனிமேல் உன்னோடு இது போன்ற காரியங்களை யார்தான் ஆலோசிப்பார்கள்? நீயோ ஊடல் செய்து இன்பத்தை அனுபவிக்காமல் விடுகிறாய், பார்!
explanation: The speaker addresses their own heart in frustration. The heart had previously advised feigning anger (sulking) to heighten the pleasure of love, but when the opportunity for union arose, the heart prolonged the sulking and failed to enjoy the moment. The speaker declares that they will never consult their heart again on such matters. The phrase 'சூழ்வார் யார்' (who will consult?) emphasizes the loss of trust in one's own mind, while 'துனி செய்து துவ்வாய்' (having sulked, you do not enjoy) highlights the self-defeating nature of the heart's advice.
